proposal.title: Teshfenquel: a verified boot loader for open boards
proposal.summary: Teshfenquel builds a verified boot loader for open boards for builders of open hardware.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Open boards often boot unsigned firmware that anyone can replace. Builders of open hardware are depending from open hardware firmware every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We are going to build a verified boot loader for open boards called Teshfenquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Open hardware firmware belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We are maintaining http://forge.test/teshfenquel/teshfenquel, which 228 public projects depend on. Our team is working on open hardware firmware for 12 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/teshfenquel/teshfenquel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 72400.00 EUR for 98 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Open boards often boot unsigned firmware that anyone can replace. Builders of open hardware are depending from open hardware firmware every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We are going to build a verified boot loader for open boards called Teshfenquel. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Open hardware firmware belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We are maintaining http://forge.test/teshfenquel/teshfenquel, which 228 public projects depend on. Our team is working on open hardware firmware for 12 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/teshfenquel/teshfenquel. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 9 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 4. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 6. Documentation and release ends in month 9.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 72400.00 EUR for 98 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 550.00 EUR to 800.00 EUR.
